theme: 3 terms on enums: modeling choices in Swift

terms.definition: A type that lists a fixed set of related choices, called cases.
terms.example: Use an enum for the order status, and the compiler checks every case.

terms.definition: Extra data stored inside one case of an enum, so each case can carry its own details.
terms.example: Add an associated value to the card case, so it keeps the last four digits.

terms.definition: A fixed number or text that each enum case is created with, such as 1 or "low".
terms.example: Give each level a raw value, so we can save it as a number.

video.title: Enum, Associated Value & Raw Value in 2 minutes | iOS Daily English Day 7
video.description:
Learn to talk about enums in Swift: Enum, Associated Value and Raw Value, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Enum - A type that lists a fixed set of related choices, called cases.
Associated Value - Extra data stored inside one case of an enum, so each case can carry its own details.
Raw Value - A fixed number or text that each enum case is created with, such as 1 or "low".

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 7 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

landscape.title: Swift Enum, Associated Value & Raw Value in English | Order Status Chat | Day 7
landscape.description:
Explain Enum, Associated Value and Raw Value in Swift by listening to a real status-screen chat between two iOS devs.
열거형, 연관 값, 원시 값 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Enum - A type that lists a fixed set of related choices, called cases.
한국어: 정해진 선택지(케이스)를 모아 둔 타입

Associated Value - Extra data stored inside one case of an enum, so each case can carry its own details.
한국어: 열거형 케이스 안에 함께 저장하는 추가 데이터

Raw Value - A fixed number or text that each enum case is created with, such as 1 or "low".
한국어: 열거형 케이스마다 미리 정해 둔 고정 숫자나 문자열

In this video, Mina and Jake build an order status screen in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Jake, why do you have status typos?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I use five strings. Try an enum: it lists every status in one place.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Write `case paid` and `case shipped`, and you cannot misspell them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. But shipped needs a tracking number.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then add an associated value to that case.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, an associated value is extra data inside one case.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So `shipped(tracking: String)` has an associated value, and `paid` has none.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Now the server sends numbers like 1 and 2 for the status.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then use a raw value. Write `enum Status: Int`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hmm, I tried that with an associated value, and it failed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right, my mistake. An enum with associated values cannot have a raw value.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So I make two enums: one for the server, one for the screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good plan. Use `rawValue` to turn the server number into a case.
Give each level a raw value, so we can save it.
